content (text): Achieving a Band 7 or higher in IELTS Writing requires more than just good English skills. It demands a clear understanding of the scoring criteria, proper essay structure, and consistent practice with targeted feedback. The IELTS Writing test consists of two tasks. In Task 1, you must describe a chart, graph, table, or diagram in at least 150 words. In Task 2, you need to write an essay of at least 250 words responding to a given prompt. Both tasks are graded on four criteria: Task Achievement, Coherence and Cohesion, Lexical Resource, and Grammatical Range and Accuracy. To score Band 7+, you need to present a clear position throughout your essay, use a range of complex sentence structures, and demonstrate precise vocabulary. Avoid common mistakes such as using contractions in formal writing, failing to address all parts of the prompt, or not providing supporting examples for your arguments. title: Scholarship Opportunities for International Medical Students in 2025
excerpt: A comprehensive overview of the best scholarships available for students pursuing medical degrees abroad, including fully-funded programs, merit-based awards, and country-specific grants.
content (text):
Funding your medical education abroad can seem daunting, but numerous scholarship opportunities exist specifically for international students. In this guide, we explore the most impactful scholarships and grants that can significantly reduce or even eliminate the financial burden of studying medicine overseas.

Fully-Funded Government Scholarships

Several governments offer fully-funded scholarships for international medical students. The Georgian Government Scholarship Program provides tuition waivers for outstanding international students enrolled in accredited medical universities. Similarly, countries like Turkey, Poland, and Romania offer government-sponsored scholarships that cover tuition, accommodation, and monthly stipends for selected candidates.

University-Specific Merit Awards

Many medical universities have their own merit-based scholarship programs. Tbilisi State Medical University offers the International Excellence Award, which provides partial tuition coverage ranging from 20% to 50% based on academic achievement. The University of Georgia runs a similar program for students maintaining a GPA above 3.5. These awards are typically renewable each year, provided the student continues to meet the academic requirements.

Regional and International Organizations

Organizations such as the World Health Organization (WHO), the Islamic Development Bank (IsDB), and the Aga Khan Foundation offer scholarships and educational grants for students from developing countries pursuing medical degrees abroad. The IsDB Scholarship Program, for instance, covers full tuition, living expenses, and even provides a monthly allowance for medical students from member countries.

How to Maximize Your Chances

Start your scholarship search at least 6-12 months before your intended enrollment date. Prepare a compelling personal statement, secure strong recommendation letters, and maintain excellent academic records. Many scholarships also value community involvement and leadership experience, so document your extracurricular activities thoroughly. title: Cost of Living in Georgia: A Student Budget Breakdown
excerpt: A detailed breakdown of monthly expenses for international students in Georgia — including accommodation, food, transport, and entertainment.
content (text):
One of the biggest advantages of studying in Georgia is the affordable cost of living. In this article, we break down the typical monthly expenses for an international student living in Tbilisi.

Accommodation: $200 - $500/month

Student housing options range from university dormitories ($150-250/month) to private apartments ($300-500/month). Shared apartments are the most popular option, offering privacy and comfort at a reasonable price. Most apartments come fully furnished with all necessary amenities.

Food and Groceries: $150 - $250/month

Georgia is famous for its cuisine, and eating out is incredibly affordable. A meal at a local restaurant costs between $3-8, while cooking at home can reduce your food budget significantly. Local markets offer fresh produce at very low prices.

Transportation: $20 - $40/month

Tbilisi has an excellent public transportation system including buses and the metro. A monthly transit pass costs around $15. Taxis are also very affordable, with most rides within the city costing $2-5.

Health Insurance: $30 - $60/month

International students are required to have health insurance. Several affordable options are available specifically designed for students, covering doctor visits, hospital stays, and emergency care.

Total Monthly Budget: $400 - $850

With careful planning, a student can live comfortably in Tbilisi for $500-600 per month, making it one of the most affordable student cities in Europe.

title: How to Get Your Medical Degree Recognized Internationally
excerpt: A step-by-step guide to licensing and recognizing your Georgian medical degree in the UAE, UK, USA, and other countries.
content (text):
One of the most common concerns for students considering studying medicine abroad is degree recognition. This guide explains how graduates from Georgian medical universities can practice medicine in various countries around the world.

United Arab Emirates (UAE)

The UAE Ministry of Education requires degree attestation, which involves verifying your degree with the Georgian Ministry of Education, followed by UAE embassy attestation. After that, you will need to pass the UAE licensing exam (DHA, DOH, or MOH) to practice medicine.

United Kingdom (PLAB)

Graduates from WHO-listed medical schools (which includes accredited Georgian universities) are eligible to take the PLAB test. Passing both parts of PLAB allows you to register with the GMC and practice medicine in the UK.

United States (USMLE)

Georgian medical graduates are eligible to take the USMLE (United States Medical Licensing Examination). After passing all three steps and completing a residency program, you can practice medicine in the US.

European Union

Medical degrees from accredited Georgian universities are recognized in many EU countries, though some may require additional language proficiency tests or bridging courses.
